sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The **Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016** provides the statutory backing for the management of funds collected for compensatory afforestation.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: **Net Present Value (NPV)** is the monetary value calculated for the loss of forest ecosystem services, which the user agency must pay.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: The **Polluter Pays Principle** dictates that the entity diverting forest land must bear the cost of restoring forest cover elsewhere.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Funds are split as **90% to States** and **10% to the Centre**.

items.definition: Mandatory afforestation on non-forest land (or degraded forest land) equivalent to the area diverted for non-forest use.
Legislation that established the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund (under Public Account of India) and State Funds (under Public Account of States).

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Key Application 1**: Artificial regeneration, assisted natural regeneration, and forest fire prevention.
• **Key Application 2**: Soil and moisture conservation works and wildlife management.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Diversion of funds for non-forestry purposes, lack of transparency in site selection, and monoculture plantations.
• **Solutions**: Use of GIS/Remote sensing for monitoring, focus on indigenous species, and community-led forest management.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: '90-10-NPV'
• **Decoded Meaning**: 90% goes to States, 10% to Centre, and NPV is the core calculation metric for the fund.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often claims CAMPA funds are part of the Consolidated Fund of India. They are actually part of the Public Account of India.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Ecological Compensation' to describe CAMPA in the context of balancing infrastructure development with environmental integrity.

keyTakeaways: CAMPA is governed by the CAF Act, 2016, not just executive orders.
Funds are held in the Public Account, not the Consolidated Fund.
The primary objective is to offset the loss of forest land through mandatory compensatory afforestation.
